points.t: **Persistent scaly salmon-pink patches** or thin plaques on buttocks, hips, trunk or breasts that **never quite clear** despite steroids.
**Skin-homing clonal helper T cells**; slow patch → plaque → tumour; **Sézary syndrome** is the leukaemic form with erythroderma.
Suspect, **stop repeated empirical treatment**, refer for multiple biopsies; specialist skin-directed therapy for early disease.
**Tumour-stage disease**, **erythroderma with nodes (Sézary)**, years of misdiagnosis as eczema or psoriasis.

cause.lead: A slow lymphoma living in the skin.
points: Clonal **CD4+** memory T cells (often CD7−, CD26−); cause unknown.
Hallmarks: **epidermotropism without spongiosis**, **Pautrier microabscesses**: often absent early.
Usually **indolent**: stage IA has near-normal life expectancy.

visuals.caption: Mycosis fungoides progresses slowly: patch (few atypical T cells in the epidermis) → plaque (more cells, thicker) → tumour (dermal nodule packed with lymphoma cells).
visuals.alt: Three skin sections showing patch, plaque and tumour stages

points: **Patch**: finely wrinkled (‘cigarette-paper’) pink-brown patches in **bathing-trunk** sites (buttocks, hips, breasts, inner thighs); itchy or not; **steroid-resistant or relapsing**.
**Plaque**: infiltrated, scaly, annular. **Tumour**: nodules that may ulcerate.
Variants: folliculotropic, **hypopigmented** (skin of colour, children), granulomatous slack skin, pagetoid reticulosis.
**Multiple**, ideally after a **2–4-week steroid washout**; IHC + **TCR gene rearrangement**.
Early MF needs **≥ 4 points** (clinical, histology, molecular, immunopathology).

manage.lead: Recognise failure to respond and refer.

points: Rash not responding to an appropriate **potent topical steroid over several weeks**, esp. sun-protected sites → biopsy. **Don’t escalate indefinitely.**
Routine → urgent by stage clues; managed by **supra-network skin lymphoma MDTs**.
Consider stopping a suspected culprit (e.g. amlodipine) and reviewing at 6–12 weeks, jointly with GP / dermatology.
Skin-directed: topical steroids, phototherapy; advanced disease: systemic therapy.

limits.t: Biopsy atypical adult-onset ‘eczema’ before biologics: CTCL can be unmasked.

items.t: Fixed patches or plaques in sun-protected sites failing treatment for months: biopsy.
**Erythroderma with lymph nodes**, intense itch, weight loss: **Sézary syndrome**.
Tumours or ulcerated nodules in known or suspected MF.

pearls.t: ‘Eczema’ in **bathing-trunk** sites that never clears → biopsy.
Early MF is usually **chronic and indolent**: avoid ‘advanced cancer’ framing before staging.
Repeat biopsies are often needed; diagnosis can take years.

quiz.a: Multiple biopsies after a 2–4-week steroid washout.

quiz.q: Why biopsy before dupilumab in atypical adult eczema?
quiz.a: CTCL can be unmasked or accelerated.
